source_text: Interim per dies plurimos effusione sanguinis transmittebatur ad dominum numerosa fraternitas, nec peruenire ad Mariani et Iacobi clericorumque uictimam rabies insanientis praesidis poterat, laicorum tam multis occupata uulneribus. Nam ita inter se nostrae religionis gradus artifex saeuitia diuiserat, ut laicos a clericis separatos temptationibus saeculi et terroribus suis putaret esse cessuros. Ergo carissimi nostri et fidelissimi milites Christi ceterique de clero contristari aliquantulum coeperant, quod, laicis certaminis sui laude perfunctis, seruaretur sibi tam lenta et tam sera uictoria.
thought_title: Lay Christians die first while clergy wait
orientation: The narrator explains the delay in prison while many lay Christians are executed before Marian, James and the other clergy.
pass_a_gloss: Meanwhile through many days by outpouring of blood a numerous brotherhood was being sent over to the Lord, and the mad rage of the raving governor was not able to reach to the victim of Marian and James and of the clerics, being occupied with so many wounds of laymen. For artful cruelty had so divided the ranks of our religion among themselves, that it supposed that laymen separated from clerics would yield to the temptations of the world and to its own terrors. Therefore our dearest and most faithful soldiers of Christ and the rest from the clergy had begun to be saddened a little, because, with laymen having fully discharged the praise of their own contest, so slow and so late a victory was being kept back for themselves.

choices.why: literal sacrificial victim for the coming execution, not yet a general death

choices.english: mad rage of the raving governor
choices.why: keeps both nouns of madness and brief glossary term governor
gradus is military or clerical rank distinction between laymen and clergy

choices.english: having fully discharged the praise of their own contest
choices.why: keeps ablative absolute and laus as praise won, not crown

pass_b_english: Meanwhile, over the course of many days, a great company of our brothers was sent over to the Lord through the outpouring of blood, while the mad rage of the raving governor could not reach its victim in Marian and James and the clergy, because it was still busy with the wounds of so many laymen. For a calculating cruelty had divided the ranks of our religion from one another, supposing that laymen, once separated from the clergy, would yield to the temptations of the world and to its own terrors. So our dearest and most faithful soldiers of Christ and the rest of the clergy began to grow somewhat sorrowful, since the laymen were having fully discharged the praise of their own contest, while so slow and so late a victory was being held back for them.
